rules:
When creating or organizing nodes in a Unity Prefab, if a node or its component will be accessed dynamically at runtime (e.g., via script binding, event callbacks, or data-driven updates), you MUST name the node using the corresponding prefix from the Script Generate Rule table below. This ensures automatic script generation compatibility.

Script Generate Rule Table:
m_go → GameObject
m_item → Transform
m_tf → Transform
m_rect → RectTransform
m_tmp → TextMeshProUGUI
m_txt → Text
m_richTxt → RichTextItem
m_btn → Button
m_img → Image
m_rimg → RawImage
m_scrollBar → Scrollbar
m_scrollRect → ScrollRect
m_input → InputField
m_slider → Slider
m_tog → Toggle
m_group → ToggleGroup
m_curve → AnimationCurve
m_canvasGroup → CanvasGroup

Naming convention: Use the prefix (left column) as the node name prefix. For example, a Button node that needs runtime access should be named like "m_btnClose", "m_btnConfirm", etc. The prefix indicates which component type will be referenced in the generated script. If a node is purely visual and never needs runtime access, no prefix is required.
When use TMP and fill text with Chinese, use font Alibaba-PuHuiTi-Medium SDF
